extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent examiners in pharmaceutical, food, functional water, and chemical compound fields
extracted.subtask_description: Official examination guidelines for patentability, description and claim requirements, and patentability assessment (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability, public-health considerations) for inventions in pharmaceuticals, food, functional drinking water, and chemical compounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step for dosage regimen/dose as element
rubrics_metrics.description: “invention shall be evaluated, considering dosage regimen or dose as its element. Inventive step may be acknowledged only for a specific dosage regimen and dose which are deemed to be worthwhile to be protected as a patent due to prominent or heterogeneous effect for which a person skilled in the art cannot expect.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (Ex1) claim of composition with Compound A 0.5–1.0 mg once a day — closest prior art disclosed 0.5–2.5 mg orally and optimization of administration is a general technical issue, so expected efficacy means inventive step denied. (Ex2) monthly high-dose administration may be found obvious if a skilled person could easily select that regimen, unless an unexpectedly striking difference (e.g., bioavailability or long-term bone density improvement) is shown. In short: dosage/regimen can support inventive step only when an unexpected/prominent effect unpredictable to skilled person is demonstrated and supported by evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step for polymorphic/crystalline forms
rubrics_metrics.description: “invention of crystal with claims stating compounds of specific crystal having different form of crystal from the compound in cited document is deemed to have the inventive step if it has different effect qualitatively or quantitatively.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is well-known that crystal form affects properties (solubility, safety, etc.) and examiners commonly review polymorphs. The effect must be stated in the description of the crystal form invention; if doubtful, effect must be proved by submitting documents such as comparative studies after filing date. A new crystal form of a known compound can be inventive if its effect is qualitatively different or quantitatively greatly different from prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Food inventions: safety and description considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: “it is necessary to determine whether the food is harmful to the health of the public or not, and unique matters including how to describe sensory effects of food and functional effects of a healthy food, and a limitation on intended use as a healthy food should be considered in examining the invention relating to food.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because food is widely accessible and consumed repeatedly, examiners must check safety of materials/components (including secondary products). If safety is unclear to a person skilled in the art, the invention may be deemed harmful to public health and rejected under Article 32. Applicants may respond with objective safety data, but adding such data may risk new matter if not supported by the original specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensory effect: requirement for objective proof
rubrics_metrics.description: “Sensory quality of food such as taste, smell, appearance, texture, etc. ... since the sense of human being can be affected by psychological or physiological condition and social background, etc., the effect of the invention cannot be determined by only personal sense of an inventor or a specific person. It is necessary to prove its effect objectively and scientifically through physiochemical or mechanical analysis, or systemic sensory test, etc.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sensory features are asserted, the description must include objective analytic methods (devices, conditions) or properly designed sensory tests. Examples of devices: colorimeter, spectrophotometer, GC, electronic nose, electronic tongue, refractometer, viscometer, texture analyzers. Provide method details so a skilled person can reproduce and quantify results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physiochemical/mechanical analysis details
rubrics_metrics.description: “The method, device, requirements, etc. should be stated specifically in the description of the invention for a skilled person in the art to understand and reproduce the invention. The detailed statement is needed to fully support sensory feature in accordance to the result of analysis.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe measurement methods, devices and parameters. Link analytical results to claimed sensory effects (e.g., Brix change for sweetness). Without specific analytical details the sensory claim may be unsupported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensory test design and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: “A method of a sensory test, number of panels, and standards of selection, etc. should be stated in the description of the invention, and the result of the test should be described with quantity; provided, however, that it should be stated clearly and in detail to support objectively the effectiveness.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sensory tests when instrumental analysis is absent/uncorrelated or when effects are complex (masking, bitterness reduction, preference). Describe panel selection, training, test protocol, and quantitative results demonstrating distinguishable effects versus controls and prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional effect of food: evidence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: “Food has useful functions for health such as improvement of health or prevention of disease, etc. Those functions or new functions shall be stated in detail and clearly confirmed by using various ways including experiment in vitro, animal testing, clinical test, or biomarker, which can support its effectiveness.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If function is already publicly known and effective dose is sufficient to identify function, re-proving may be unnecessary. Otherwise provide objective test results (in vitro, animal, clinical, biomarker) and ensure composition contains effective dosage; otherwise examiner may raise deficiency of description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims for health functional foods — usage treated as claim element
rubrics_metrics.description: “If the subject matter recited in a claim is a health functional food, the usage limiting the food is considered as a claim element.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a usage limitation in a claim to restrict a food may be treated as an element; however, merely stating a different usage for the same composition as prior art does not automatically impart novelty (see note referencing case law).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims for health functional foods — describe usage by objective
rubrics_metrics.description: “For a use invention of a health functional food, its usage shall be specifically described by not its quality itself but its objectives to be achieved through the quality.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State specific objectives (e.g., improvement of hyperlipidemia, reduction of blood sugar) rather than ambiguous quality terms. Quality terms that describe mechanism/function rather than use may not be accepted as a use-limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims for health functional foods — permitted scope of usage expression
rubrics_metrics.description: “Contrary to a medicinal use invention stating a usage for cure of specific diseases or symptoms, the usage may be stated with the type of function which is helpful to human body.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid claiming food as a medicinal treatment (e.g., 'to treat disease'); such phrasing is unclear/ improper because food is not a medicinal object. Use appropriate wording that reflects health-promoting function rather than treatment of disease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpatentable food inventions: specific cases
rubrics_metrics.description: “Where safety of food material or its compound is not clear to a person skilled in the art, the invention is deemed harmful to public health. Therefore, examiner shall give a notice of grounds for rejection under Article 32 of Patent Act.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of unpatentable cases: new material never consumed as food; prohibited for use as food due to harmfulness in government/authority reports or databases; harmfulness reported in academic journals; descriptions (intake volume, route) beyond scientific knowledge. Applicant may submit safety reports to rebut but beware of new-matter rules when amending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional drinking water: description and evidentiary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: “it is necessary to satisfy requirements for description including statement of medical effect of functional drinking water, statement of maintaining magnetic state of magnetized water, etc.; subject matter eligibility of invention, and determine whether the invention is possibly harmful to public health or not pursuant to Article 32 of Patent Act.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For electrolyzed reduced water, state process parameters and beneficial effects; for hexagonal water and magnetized water, submit objective tests and measurement methods to support production principle and claimed states. If medical effects are asserted, provide objective data unless the effect is part of technical common knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability / completed invention requirement for functional water
rubrics_metrics.description: “Since manufacturing device or manufacturing method of hexagonal water made by Hyranya (hexagonal pyramid) model has no test reports or evidence to prove that hexagonal water is just made by Hyranya model, it is considered as uncompleted invention which is impossible to be accomplished.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processes that are theoretical without scientific proof or lacking evidence to show the claimed result are uncompleted and may be ineligible. Demonstrate practicability with test data or reproducible methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical compound: characterization and synthetic procedure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: “Confirmatory data to identify compounds and the preparation (synthetic procedure) shall be stated in the description of the invention.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide compound characterization (elemental analysis, NMR, melting/boiling points) and preparation methods. For polymorphs provide XRD, DSC, IR, and/or chemical/physical data. If preparation is non-trivial or side reactions expected, include sufficient experimental detail so a skilled person can prepare the compound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical compound: requirement to disclose representative embodiments
rubrics_metrics.description: “For an invention relating to a new chemical compound, embodiment specifying technical means shall be disclosed. Where the claim is recited genetically, representative embodiment shall be disclosed by a group except for a case that the specific content of invention can be recognized to a person skilled in the art based on the disclosure of the specification and the level of skill in the art.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using broad/Markush-type claims, disclose representative examples and embodiments to support the claimed genus; failure to do so may lead to a finding that the claim is not supported by the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be supported by the description
rubrics_metrics.description: “If in a claim a chemical compound is expressed as Markush type having multiple elements, and only a detailed example of preparing compound with specific structure frame is stated in the description, if it is considered that compound with other structure frames is not clearly understood by a person skilled in the art, an examiner shall notify the grounds for rejection that claimed invention is not supported by the description…”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claim scope is commensurate with disclosed examples; explain why the broader claim is enabled or narrow the claim to supported embodiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of chemical compound claims (naming, formulae, properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: “If a new chemical compound is specified by its name, or structural formula, the claim shall be deemed clear. ... If structural formula is simple, it will be possible to state only the name ... if physical or chemical property can specify it, it is allowed to define the invention with the properties.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify name, structural formula, and crystal structure when needed. Use property-based definitions only when they uniquely identify the compound. Avoid ambiguous terms like 'substituted …' without specifying substituents, and be cautious using generic labels ('alkyl', 'aryl') if carbon-number range or embodiments require specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty rules for chemical compounds (specific characteristics, salts, purity)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Chemical compound defined by specific characteristics ... if the claimed compound is identical with the well-known compound specified by name or structural formula, the claimed compound is deemed to lack novelty. A chemical compound and its conventional salt are substantially identical. Hence the salt of the known compound is deemed to lack novelty. A known chemical compound with simply improved purity lacks novelty.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid claiming known compounds by only changing naming conventions, salts, or marginal purity improvements unless distinctive properties or structure are shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of preparation method (method claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Where the claimed preparation method is the same with that of the prior art, and merely the use is limited, it is deemed to lack novelty since both are preparations for producing the substantially same compound.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method claims that are identical to prior art except for a use limitation will generally lack novelty. Using a starting material produced by a particular prior preparation may also render the method non-novel if other conditions are equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step for chemical compound inventions (structure + special effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Inventive step of a chemical compound invention is determined by two features: i) structural formula ii) technically special effect of the chemical compound. ... improved effects accomplished by the claimed compound compared to that of a prior art reference is very important ... An examiner should not deny the inventive step because of similar structure ... if the claimed compound has unexpected or extraordinary characteristic, it is recognized as involving inventive step.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the claimed structural differences and/or unexpected technical advantages (final result, chemical feature, purpose or use) would have been predictable to a skilled person. If effects are predictable, inventive step may be denied despite favorable results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step for inorganic compounds with specific features
rubrics_metrics.description: “For an inorganic compound, even though the name and the chemical formula are same, it is common that physical property or its configuration, including microstructure such as crystal form, a unit surface area of particles, etc. is different. ... to determine inventive step of the invention of preparation of inorganic compound with specific feature, the review of specific property shall be included in the claim regardless of statement of the property.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should specify the specific properties (microstructure, particle surface area, etc.) that distinguish the inorganic product; the claim should allow review of whether those properties are produced by the claimed combination of components and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-by-use claims (use limitation construed as utility, not novelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: “In case of a chemical compound, use of which is limited by stating ‘for~’ (e.g. Chemical compound Z for Y), since the limitation is just to indicate its utility, so it is considered as a chemical compound without use limitation (e.g. Chemical compound Z). If a claimed chemical compound is disclosed in the prior art, the chemical compound with use limitation is deemed to lack novelty.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim of product 'for' a use will typically be read as the product per se for novelty purposes. To obtain novelty for a new use, consider use-limited method claims or other claim drafting strategies; be aware of local case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection invention: species must show qualitative/quantitative difference
rubrics_metrics.description: “In order for selection invention involving novelty over the prior art invention disclosing only the generic concept to be recognized involving inventive step over the prior art, all the species included in the selection invention should have different effect from that of the prior art invention qualitatively or quantitatively.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection of specific species from a broad genus requires demonstrating that the selected species exhibit distinguishing effects (qualitative or quantitative) not predictable from the generic disclosure. Mere arbitrary selection among a wide range without special effects will lack inventive step.
